title: Will the hottest range stay inside its budget?
description: Change the key shape, range count, node count, and peak write rate. The model separates comfortable cluster averages from the ownership range that actually receives the most writes.

strategies.label: Sequential primary key
strategies.detail: New rows converge on the final key interval even after older ranges split.
strategies.tradeoff: Ordered scans stay local, but the active tail range limits peak writes.

strategies.label: Random UUID primary key
strategies.detail: Point writes spread across the existing keyspace instead of one active tail.
strategies.tradeoff: Point distribution improves, but time-ordered access needs a separate index whose own leading key must be reviewed.

strategies.label: 8-bucket hash-sharded key
strategies.detail: A computed prefix spreads a sequential logical key across a bounded number of write fronts.
strategies.tradeoff: The hot tail is divided, but scans by logical order merge results from up to eight buckets.

notice: Illustrative pressure model only. Replace the capacity constants with measured limits for the real schema, indexes, row size, transaction mix, storage, replication placement, and background work.
